manual_verification.reason: Read-only semantic refinement; no runtime or gameplay mutation.

prohibitions: Do not invent reminder text, scheduler cadence, retry policy, opt-out policy, or batch limits.
Do not equate candidate selection with successful Telegram delivery.
Do not record a successful reminder before delivery succeeds.
Do not use process-local memory as the exact-once authority.
Do not connect V2 runtime, Telegram, or production persistence during refinement.
Do not open or manipulate game.db, game.db-wal, or game.db-shm.

refined_contract.contract: A reminder becomes due only after seven full 24-hour days since canonical last_activity_at; equality at the threshold is due.
Eligibility is evaluated against an explicit timezone-aware UTC instant. Unit tests must use an injected deterministic clock, never wall-clock sleeps.
The inactivity cycle is anchored to the last_activity_at value used for eligibility. At most one successful reminder receipt may exist per user and cycle anchor.
A later canonical last_activity_at creates a distinct cycle after another seven-full-days interval; an earlier receipt must not suppress the new cycle.
Successful reminder delivery is represented by persistent inactivity_reminders evidence. In-memory flags are not authoritative across restarts.
Eligibility selection, Telegram delivery, and durable success receipt are distinct boundaries. A failed delivery must not be recorded as successfully sent.

This contract does not invent scheduler cadence, startup timing, batch size, retry backoff, concurrency locking, message text, or recipient opt-out semantics unless authoritative V1 evidence explicitly owns them.
A later implementation may create API-ready domain/service ports only after parity resolution; Telegram runtime and production persistence wiring remain out of scope until explicitly authorized.
